description: Samuel's injury occurred late in Sunday's win over Seattle

Samuel's injury occurred late in Sunday's win over Seattle

        Another day, another notable 49ers injury to monitor. This time, it's wideout Deebo Samuel, who injured his hamstring during the second half of San Francisco's Week 5 win over the Seattle Seahawks. Samuels underwent further evaluation on Monday, and 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said that Samuel will be out "at least a couple of weeks." San Francisco will host Washington next week on "Monday Night Football." It will then face the Falcons in Atlanta in Week 7 before a Week 8 bye. The injury occurred late in the third quarter with the 49ers trailing, 23-21. Samuel stayed on the ground for several moments after committing the 49ers' second turnover of the quarter. He fumbled the ball while running after a catch, and the turnover led to a Seattle field goal. 
The 49ers responded with consecutive scoring drives. The first ended with a Brock Purdy touchdown pass to Brandin Cooks, who was recently signed to help the 49ers navigate through their injuries at receiver. The second drive was capped off by Eddy Pineiro's 44-yard field goal that proved to be the game-winning score. 
San Francisco received a big game from Mike Evans, who caught seven passes for 113 yards and a score despite having two fractured ribs. 
Evans and Cooks will have to continue to pick up the slack in Samuel's absence during the next several weeks. Samuel, 30, has had a successful reunion with the 49ers, who re-signed him this offseason after he spent the 2025 season with the Commanders. He's currently tied for second on the team with three touchdown catches and is second in receptions. He also has four runs that have resulted in first downs. 
Despite their injuries, the 49ers are one of only three teams that are still undefeated. San Francisco currently has a two-game cushion over the rest of the field in the NFC West division.

title: UCLA QB Nico Iamaleava expected to miss remainder of season after knee injury - CBS Sports
description: Iamaleava exited Saturday's win over Oregon after suffering an apparent leg injury
body:
Iamaleava exited Saturday's win over Oregon after suffering an apparent leg injury
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:19 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava is expected to miss the remainder of the season with a knee injury, sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. Iamaleava exited Saturday's 17-15 win over Oregon after getting tangled up awkwardly between a pair of Ducks defenders.At his Monday press conference, Bob Chesney admitted there was "serious concern' but didn't officially rule out Iamaleava for the rest of the season."I'm gonna wait on our doctors to make the final call on things," Chesney said. "He has a meeting later today, and we'll have a lot more clarity on where things are at. ... There is serious concern at the moment, but at the same time, there's nothing that has been fully ruled at this time. There's still other opinions and people we want to talk to just to make sure everyone sees it the same way."A former five-star recruit, Iamaleava transferred from Tennessee to UCLA prior to the 2025 season, and he stuck with the Bruins after Chesney took charge. In his second season with the Bruins, Iamaleava provided some stability at the quarterback position, even if his numbers didn't jump off the page.
In four-plus games, Iamaleava completed 62.1 percent of his passes for 982 yards, four touchdowns and four interceptions while rushing for 144 yards and a score.Looking ahead to the offseason, Iamaleava will have a big decision to make regarding the 2027 NFL Draft. Iamaleava has the tools to be an early-round selection, but he may have to spend one more season at the college level to prove his health and boost his draft stock.When Iamaleava left the game against Oregon, backup Ty Dieffenbach entered and managed the offense well enough to get the win. The senior completed three of his six passing attempts for 43 yards and a touchdown.
No. 12 UCLA's first test without Iamaleava will be a home contest against 4-1 Wisconsin on Saturday night.Where do the Bruins go at QB?While Dieffenbach replaced Iamaleava against Oregon, that doesn't mean the starting role is his for the rest of the season. In his postgame press conference, Chesney admitted it will be a "week-to-week" situation and that Dieffenbach's mobility earned him the nod as the primary back against Oregon."We're really on a week-to-week basis here," Chesney told 247Sports. "This week, we felt like we had to run a little bit more with the quarterback, possibly. And that's where I thought Ty had a really nice week. And that put us in that spot. It's just one of those things. I'm sure if Madden had gone in there, he would have done a phenomenal job as well. But Ty was the guy we decided on based on the previous week of practice, and I thought he did a really good job. But Madden is going to be there the whole way through as well, competing and fighting for that position with or without Nico."
Although he performed admirably, Dieffenbach's appearance against Oregon was his FBS debut. A three-star recruit out of high school, Dieffenbach spent two years at Pitt before transferring to Cal Poly last season. He was the Mustangs' starter last year before transferring to UCLA in the offseason.In his lone season at Cal Poly, Dieffenbach completed just 56.8 percent of his passes for 1,305 yards, nine touchdowns and nine interceptions.Dieffenbach's resume -- or lack thereof -- probably leaves the door open for sophomore Madden Iamaleava, Nico's younger brother. A four-star recruit in the 2025 signing class, Madden spent a few months at Arkansas before joining his brother at UCLA.
Madden Iamaleava has even less experience, limited to one passing attempt in his career. It fell incomplete.This may be a scenario in which Chesney simply rides the hot hand from one week to another, but the good news is that the quarterback probably won't be asked to do much.How much does QB matter?The quarterback definitely matters, since the Bruins can't play someone who derails the entire offense. But can Chesney find a game manager between Dieffenbach and Madden Iamaleava? That may be all he needs.
If Chesney can get average quarterback play the rest of the way, then UCLA's College Football Playoff hopes are very much still alive because of how good the team is at running the ball and playing defense.The Bruins rank sixth in the country in rushing yards per game with 253.2, and Wayne Knight is budding into a national superstar at running back. That should allow UCLA to take some of the burden off its quarterback, whoever that may be.It also helps that the Bruins don't need to light up the scoreboard because of how the defense is playing. The Bruins are eighth in the Big Ten in scoring defense, allowing just 18.0 points per game, and they're especially good against the run, surrendering just 87.6 rushing yards per game.
That means the quarterback doesn't have to air the ball out to win. In fact, Nico Iamaleava wasn't exactly turning heads with his play before the injury. The elder Iamaleava brother turned the ball over three times against Oregon, and UCLA still managed to pull out a win in Autzen Stadium.

title: NFL suspends 49ers Dre Greenlaw one game after head-butting incident vs. Seahawks - CBS Sports
description: The discipline stems from a second-quarter incident where
body:
The discipline stems from a second-quarter incident where the linebacker drew a late-hit flag on Sam Darnold and headbutted a helmetless Ernest Jones IV
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:34 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw has been suspended for one game without pay after he was ejected during the 49ers' 32-29 victory over the Seattle Seahawks, per the NFL. Greenlaw is scheduled to miss the 49ers' Week 6 matchup against the Washington Commanders, but he is allowed to appeal the NFL's decision. During the second quarter, Greenlaw drew a flag for a late hit on Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold on the Seattle sideline and was confronted by several Seahawks players, including linebacker Ernest Jones. As the two players met face-to-face, Greenlaw head-butted the helmetless Jones, leading to his ejection. 
"During the second quarter, Greenlaw used his helmet to headbutt Seattle linebacker Ernest Jones IV, who was not wearing a helmet, violating Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to 'any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship,'" the league said in its statement.Greenlaw has been suspended before, receiving a one-game ban last year during his stint with the Denver Broncos. That came after he aggressively ran after an official while yelling at them following a game-winning field goal. Greenlaw has also been ejected multiple times before, including in 2022 following a helmet-to-helmet hit on Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, and later that same year in the playoffs, when he threw a jab at Philadelphia Eagles head of security Dom DiSandro. 
In five games played this season, Greenlaw has recorded 37 tackles and one forced fumble.

title: Should winless Titans bench Cam Ward? Why abandoning the former No. 1 pick will not fix Tennessee's' turmoil - CBS Sports
description: Turning to Mitch Trubisky will not fix an offense averaging just 11.6 points or an expensive, revamped defense th
body:
Turning to Mitch Trubisky will not fix an offense averaging just 11.6 points or an expensive, revamped defense that has disappointed
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Tennessee Titans fell to 0-5 on Sunday after being handily defeated by their rival, the Houston Texans, 26-3. The Texans were also winless heading into this matchup, but they used the hapless Titans as a get-right game. Tennessee is a disaster, in more ways than one. This was the top team in the AFC just five years ago. Now, the Titans are unrecognizable. No, literally — they are unrecognizable. The Titans debuted new uniforms, created a new logo, and found new ways to disappoint everyone in Nashville.Reporters who have covered this franchise since the move to the Volunteer State in 1997 claim this is as bad as it's ever been, and it's hard to disagree with that assessment. The Titans are now 6-33 over the past three seasons and 2-18 at home. Both rank worst in the NFL. You read that correctly, by the way. The Titans have won two home games over the last three years. The last victory in front of their home fans came against a Chris Oladokun-led Kansas City Chiefs team last season. Titans players and coaches have talked about "owning the (AFC) south." Tennessee is 2-20 in its past 22 divisional games, the worst record over that span since the 2008-2012 Cleveland Browns. 
A major talking point when it comes to this "Titanic" disaster is the play of the quarterback. Former No. 1 overall pick Cam Ward has not looked like a legitimate starter through five games, and he's entering some pretty dangerous historical territory as the losses mount. Ward is now 3-19 as an NFL starter. It's the second-worst QB record through 22 starts all-time, behind Steve DeBerg (2-20).
Maybe wins aren't a legitimate QB stat, but through five games, Ward ranks 28th in both passer rating (77.2) and passing yards per game (179.2). He's thrown just three touchdowns. Jaxson Dart had three passing touchdowns in his one full game played this season. The "bench Cam Ward" movement has picked up steam over the past 24 hours, but head coach Robert Saleh quickly dismissed the idea of sitting his second-year signal-caller. 
"Cam's our starting quarterback," Saleh told reporters on Sunday. "We're gonna give him every opportunity to be successful this year. We're gonna continue working with him, grinding with him and trying to help him get better."Should the Titans bench Ward after five games? No. I don't think they should, and here's why: 1. It's not just Cam WardAs we exit Week 5, the Titans rank dead last in total offense (246.4 yards per game), dead last in scoring offense (11.6 points per game), and second-worst in passing offense (163.8 yards per game). No, your eyes aren't lying to you, the Titans stink. However, it's not just their quarterback.
This isn't a 2025 Minnesota Vikings situation, where Kevin O'Connell was forced to make a change under center because it was the one thing holding his team back. The Vikings had a top-three defense and a talented supporting cast ready to take off. The Titans don't have a Brian Flores defense or a Justin Jefferson. Benching Ward for Mitch Trubisky doesn't turn you into a playoff team. Against the Texans, Ward completed 23 of 36 passes for 170 yards and one interception. He was bad, but his offensive line got absolutely WORKED. It was upsetting because the play of the offensive line through four weeks was one of the few bright spots for the Titans. Not on Sunday. That bright spot was blotted out by one of the best defensive lines in the NFL, which took over this game. Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter combined for four sacks and five QB hits. Left tackle Dan Moore Jr. had maybe the worst game of his Titans career, right tackle JC Latham lost reps against his former Alabama teammate, and paying Peter Skoronski all that money in the offseason didn't make any difference. 
The Titans' entire offensive operation on Sunday was abysmal, from passing to blocking to running to even catching. Putting Trubisky in is not fixing all of this.Defensive woesThen what about the defense? Saleh is regarded as one of the best defensive minds in football, and the Titans celebrated his arrival by completely revamping that side of the ball. Tennessee paired Jeffery Simmons with new running mates on the interior, such as John Franklin-Myers, Jordan Elliott and Solomon Thomas. At pass rusher, the Titans traded for another former Saleh player in Jermaine Johnson II and drafted Keldric Faulk late in the first round. The Titans also added two new starters at cornerback in Alontae Taylor and Cor'Dale Flott. I'm not sure any of these additions have panned out just yet.Through five weeks, the Titans rank No. 19 in total defense (331.8 yards allowed per game), tied for 10th-worst in sacks (10), eighth-worst in EPA per play (.03), tied for last in takeaways and rank dead last in total defensive pressures (44). The defense has been disappointing all year.
During the Week 1 loss to the New York Jets, there was a second-quarter drive in which the Jets rushed 15 times on their way to a field goal. They picked up 74 yards on 19 plays and took up 11:48 of game time. That's called imposing your will. In Week 2 against the Philadelphia Eagles, Jalen Hurts and Co. converted on 12 of their 19 combined third and fourth downs. That same Eagles team went 0-12 on third downs vs. the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4. Then, during the Titans' matchup against the Baltimore Ravens last week, Lamar Jackson completed 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in the first two quarters. He didn't need to take the field in the second half because the 24-7 lead he built was enough to win the game. Spotrac claims the Titans spent the most money in free agency this offseason ($319,877,500). You would never be able to tell by the play on the field. I'm not defending Ward's play, which, again, has been bad, sad, disappointing — whatever descriptor you want to use. What I contend is that he's not the only problem on a very bad team. 
2. You're abandoning the season mission five weeks inThe Titans have registered four losing seasons in a row, including two straight 3-14 campaigns. What was the goal for the franchise this year with a new head coach in Saleh and a new offensive coordinator in Brian Daboll? To me, the answer to that question was easy: Find out what you have in Cam Ward.This season was all about figuring out what you have at quarterback. You can't do that with him on the bench. There are fans out there totally ready to give up on Ward and punt on their former No. 1 overall pick after 22 games. That would be an emotional decision. I actually thought Ward put together his best game of the season just eight days ago in Baltimore, throwing for 222 yards, one touchdown and an interception that wasn't his fault, while rookie Carnell Tate enjoyed a breakout performance with 145 yards receiving. Maybe there was a disconnect with some people about the expectations for the Titans this season? You had Kyle Brandt on national television riling up the fan base by picking them to make the playoffs for some reason. I was expecting a "6-11"- type season from the Titans this year, so I can agree it's looked worse than I thought it would. But do you really want to pull the plug on the Ward experiment right now? Why not accumulate all the data you can before banishing him from Music City?
CBS Sports senior NFL writer Pete Prisco said on Sunday that Ward deserves the rest of the season to prove what he can do. But if he continues to play like one of the worst quarterbacks in the NFL, then yes, Tennessee will once again hop on the QB carousel. 
Will Cam Ward eventually get benched?Ward should not be benched after a 0-5 start, but I can admit that a benching could be coming.It's easy for me to sit back and act like this is my "Madden" video game. "Let's sim to next year and draft Jeremiah Smith." The fact of the matter is, people's jobs are on the line. Being an employee of the Titans is an incredibly scary thought. It feels like those people don't have any job security. Seriously, the team just fired the executive who oversaw the entire rebrand that debuted this offseason. Brian Callahan was allowed to coach the Titans for 23 games before he was handed his walking papers. How long of a leash does Saleh have? 
If we get to the point where the Titans are 0-9 and Ward is looking totally lost on the field, then yes, a benching is warranted. I'm just not abandoning what I would consider the season mission to figure out what I have in Ward five games in.

title: Man City win shows why Premier League needs a fast resolution to financial violations - CBS Sports
description: With 19 rivals demanding clarity over looming penalties, a
body:
With 19 rivals demanding clarity over looming penalties, a drawn-out appeal and legal fight could throw the entire table into uncertainty for months
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:53 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        With their 3-0 win at Anfield on Sunday afternoon, Manchester City took a resounding early step along a path that could end in a Premier League title. Or they afforded themselves a significant boost in their battle against relegation. Maybe they achieved nothing more than to harm the prospects of great rivals Liverpool, with City's season to be defined by the sentencing commission and an appeal process.  The question for the Premier League as a whole is not only what the shape of the table might be at the end of the disciplinary process, but when that process might be concluded. Every one of the other 19 clubs finds itself in limbo to some extent. A points deduction could change everything from the title race to the relegation picture. The English game is rapidly approaching its autumn sacking season. How can executives know the appropriate response to make when there might only be two relegation spots to worry about or one more Champions League berth than usual?  It is for that reason that many in the league are emphasizing the value of a swift resolution. That was a widespread belief before this weekend's games, and it will only have grown stronger in the aftermath of City's second-half rally and the boisterous celebrations of players and fans who seemed to revel in their new status.
        
            
                'Cheats' banners, then a beatdown: Man City crush Liverpool at Anfield in first game since guilty verdict
                
                    Francesco Porzio                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick expressed that view on Friday, telling his pre-match press conference: "The sooner it gets sorted, I think for everyone's benefit, is essential." Privately that is a view echoed by other head coaches and executives, according to CBS Sports sources.  The extent to which anyone might get their wish is unclear. The Premier League can impress on both the independent commission, which will decide the extent of the sanction, and the appeal body the need for this process to be resolved quickly. Manchester City's appeal is said to refer to the damage done to the original case by an onerous timescale of over three years. Equally, the timescale is decided by the judges who have been appointed to reach a verdict.  The Premier League's current rules state that an appeal process must be concluded within 12 weeks of it being lodged, with the hearing of the appeal itself to take no more than five days. However, those rules were implemented amid the lengthy delays around the independent commission. It could be argued that City should be judged by the rules in place when they were charged, which would afford them an undetermined timeline.  The sanctioning process is understood to be able to run separately from the appeal, though both the Premier League and City could also ask for that to be reviewed if they are unhappy with its conclusions. And that is to say nothing of the last avenue that might emerge for City: challenging the league in the High Court.  All of which is to say that there are no guarantees that those who want a quick resolution will get their wish. With so many steps yet to be taken, the warping of the Premier League table has only just begun.

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline: Five big-name candidates, including Khalil Mack - CBS Sports
description: The winless Chargers have little reason to retain Mack, an aging pass rusher on an expiring contract who could he
body:
The winless Chargers have little reason to retain Mack, an aging pass rusher on an expiring contract who could help a playoff contender
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        There have been four in-season trades since the 2026 NFL campaign kicked off five weeks ago, and each of them involved a big-name player. Former Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is the most recent mover with the NFC West's last-place team sending him to the Houston Texans, and he joined Cam Jurgens, Joey Porter Jr. and J.J. McCarthy as those to be dealt ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.More transactions are on the way, with less than a month to go until the deadline. The time of year has arrived at which teams have to decide whether to spend on impact players who can help them win right now or to sell off their best assets and look ahead to the future. Veterans on expiring contracts playing for bad teams are always the likeliest to be dealt in-season, and there are a number of them who come to mind after the first quarter of the 2026 season.Some trades may not move the needle all that much. Others will feature star players or prospects like Harrison who may deliver breakout seasons with new teams.Here are five players with at least one career Pro Bowl selection who could be next in line to be traded.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Khalil Mack, EDGE, ChargersThe Chargers' season went down the drain before it ever really started. They were supposed to open the year at 2-0 before embarking on a gauntlet of a schedule, but they dropped both of those games as favorites and still have not won a game in five tries. Since things are clearly not working in Los Angeles, it might be time for a complete reboot. And even if they do not tear everything down, Khalil Mack still makes loads of sense as a trade candidate.Mack is 35 years old but on pace for his most sacks since 2023, when he finished ninth in Defensive Player of the Year voting. This might be one of the Chargers' last chances to trade him for something meaningful, especially since he is on a one-year contract. There is no guarantee he returns in 2026, and if he does, the Chargers cannot bank on him playing like this again. A playoff team would be better suited to benefit from Mack's late-career efforts than one still searching for its first victory.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jerry Jeudy, WR, BrownsSurprisingly, with three wins in five games, the Browns are not in a position to move their veterans for more draft picks. All of the youth they acquired in the last few drafts is beginning to pay off. But what if there was a way for them to secure even more draft capital without losing any meaningful production from a lineup that has been better than expected? That would be a reality if they put Jerry Jeudy on the trade block.
At 27 years old and two years removed from a 1,229-yard Pro Bowl season, Jeudry still has value. He would be a starting-caliber wide receiver on a number of teams. The Browns are simply no longer a fit for him as they commit more to their younger options like rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, who are tied for the team lead in targets. Jeudy has just two starts on the year, and his eight receptions are only the sixth-most on the roster. It looks as though Cleveland is phasing out a player it signed to a $52.5 million deal in 2024. He should have a market among teams in search of receiving depth.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tony Pollard, RB, TitansThe offense in Tennessee is a mess. There are only a couple of obvious building blocks on that unit in quarterback Cam Ward and wide receiver Carnell Tate, while just about everyone else faces an uncertain future. Tony Pollard, at 29, is significantly older than those two foundational pieces, is in the last year of an affordable contract and is not quite as productive as he was in his first two seasons with the Titans. That profile makes him a potential mover as the franchise all but certainly looks to stockpile more draft picks in the slog of a rebuild.The Titans can turn to Tyjae Spears and rookie Nicholas Singleton if they part ways with Pollard. Neither might give the offense the same kind of rushing ability that Pollard would, but that is not the point. The Titans are still in "play the long game" mode rather than in a position to flesh out a high-powered offense. A playoff-bound team could give up a draft pick to acquire Pollard as a No. 2 running back.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Josh Sweat, EDGE, CardinalsThe Cardinals already made one trade, so they are clearly keen to sell. They are still a ways out from their contention window in the loaded NFC West and need to keep stacking young difference-makers like Trey McBride and Jeremiyah Love. Moving Josh Sweat gives them an opportunity to add to their stash of draft picks, which just got even more robust with the acquisition of a second-rounder and sixth-rounder in the Harrison trade.There was some buzz in the offseason that Sweat wanted out of Arizona. General manager Monti Ossenfort said in August that the team had no intention of trading him, and Sweat dispelled this month the narrative that he wanted a new contract. Where there is smoke, there is usually fire, so there might be something brewing behind the scenes even though all parties involved are publicly on the same page about Sweat remaining a Cardinal.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Daron Payne, DT, CommandersFollowing their botched overtime execution in Week 5, the Commanders stand in sole possession of last place in the NFC East. This has the makings of another potential lost season, rather than another step towards Super Bowl contention, with Jayden Daniels as the franchise quarterback. And while teams with standout quarterbacks on rookie contracts typically seek to add veterans rather than part with them, if Washington deems this year a lost cause, it might try and get whatever it can in return for players who are not part of the long-term future. Daron Payne could be in that group.
Payne's four-year, $90 million contract voids at the end of the season, so the Commanders have a decision to make on whether to re-sign him for a second time. In the years since they paid up to keep a then-Pro Bowler, Payne has not replicated the production of his breakout, 11.5-sack 2022 season. Me might have overstayed his welcome but could be an impactful addition to another team who would not have to pay as much to retain him in 2027 as the Commanders did four years ago.Which player will be moved first?Who becomes the next player to hit the trade market largely depends on which team pulls the plug on its season first. The Chargers might be that team, considering they are off to an 0-5 start and face a brutal schedule between now and the trade deadline with road games against the Chiefs and Rams and a home date with the Texans. Things will probably get worse before they get better in Los Angeles, so it is only a matter of time before they put their roster in motion.Mack is about as clear-cut a trade option as any player in the league, not just because of the Chargers' struggles, but also due to his status as a high-performing, aging veteran on an expiring contract. Teams will likely call about him, if they have not already. One to monitor would be the Bears, who need edge rusher help as they work toward a return to the playoffs, and who are quite familiar with Mack, considering he spent four years of his prime in Chicago.

title: PGA Tour has key calls to make as DP World Tour puts foot in ground about LIV Golf - CBS Sports
description: The Monday Tee Sheet dives into what's on Brian Rolapp's plate, which golfers starred over the weekend and how th
body:
The Monday Tee Sheet dives into what's on Brian Rolapp's plate, which golfers starred over the weekend and how the sport's landscape may change in the next two years
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp has a decision to make. For better or worse, it is one he has faced before. Just about 16 months into his tenure, Rolapp has made the impossible possible and done what many other leaders in sports leagues aspire to do: garner the support and affection of players, sponsors and fans.Rolapp has rolled out new reforms in a tight manner. Nothing ever seems rushed or reactionary. He has struck a balance between upholding traditions and letting his outside experience guide decisions that insiders might overlook.A new two-tiered PGA Tour and an adjusted Tour Championship format are key structural changes to the circuit, but nuance comes storming through the doors at PGA Tour headquarters when dealing with those who are striking the shots, especially when they aren't already under your purview. Jon Rahm made it known last week that he will be leaving whatever becomes of LIV Golf. The 2.0 version of the startup league is not of interest to the two-time major champion, leaving many to wonder where he will play in 2027. 
Conventional wisdom suggests he will find a home on the DP World Tour, serve his one-year PGA Tour suspension (from the time of his last LIV Golf start) and return stateside in 2028 when the new-look tour arrives.Thanks to his win at the 2023 Masters, Rahm would be immediately eligible for the top-level Championship Series. Talk about timely.Rolapp has never been one to take the conventional route, however. He welcomed back Brooks Koepka when the five-time major champion left LIV Golf and contacted the PGA Tour about a possible return. In doing so, he also opened the door for Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith to switch allegiances via the Returning Member Program, even though those three were still firmly under contract.
The PGA Tour will not deal with golfers until their LIV Golf contracts are void or expired. As such, Rolapp has continued to harp on the same talking points. He is focused on making the PGA Tour the best it can be, regardless of who may try to jump on board in the future.Still, the moment has come for Rolapp to make a decision. It is time to open the fridge, smell the milk and weigh the two options: take a sip or throw it in the bin immediately."I've got no idea," said Xander Schauffele when asked what track Rolapp may take. "There are 225 guys with tour cards, and if you sat down and interviewed all of them, you're going to get probably three or four boxes of how guys feel. 
"Some guys don't care, some guys are really ticked off, some guys want them to have a huge fine, some guys would let them back tomorrow. Where I stand in those boxes, I don't really know. ... I try to mind my own business most times."The Next 20There was plenty of consequential golf played this weekend, but my eyes gravitated towards the Korn Ferry Tour Championship. Perhaps it was because the site of the tournament, The Federal Club, is a golf course I played in competition before (can you believe I didn't qualify for the 2016 USGA Four-Ball?!) or because some of the names on the bubble were familiar, but nevertheless, it was the tournament that grabbed my attention.Austin Hitt went from outside the top 20 to earning his PGA Tour card thanks to his first professional victory. He was one of two players to make the move inside the number, alongside Davis Lamb. 
Hitt was No. 1 by week's end on the leaderboard, but it was Ross Steelman who was No. 1 on the Korn Ferry Tour Points List by year's end. The lengthy right-hander grabbed two wins this season, six top-five finishes and will be leading a crop of 16 rookies (out of the 20 KFT grads) onto the PGA Tour in 2027.There is a lot to like about Steelman's game (mainly his driver, both long and straight), but his demeanor and the way he carries himself are impressive. The 25-year-old is ranked No. 75 in the Official World Golf Rankings ahead of names like Max Homa and Jason Day, who saw one of his records fall thanks to Blades Brown.Brown became the youngest player to graduate from the Korn Ferry Tour at 19 years, four months and 20 days, clipping Day's mark by about seven months. Other young names to highlight include Tommy Morrison, who earned his membership 131 days after his final college round at Texas, and the fast-paced Dylan Menate.
Check out all of the Korn Ferry Tour graduates.Access grantedIt is hard to say Hitt had the biggest win of the weekend when major championship berths were on the line at the Spanish Open. Madrid native Eugenio Chacarra tried his damndest to run down his national open with some injured toes, but in the end, he was outpaced by Grant Forrest of Scotland.The Scot entered the week No. 118 on the DP World Tour and No. 296 in the OWGR, but none of that matters now as the win comes with not only a trophy and job security but invitations to Augusta National and the Old Course at St. Andrews in 2027. I've loved this move to elevate national opens even more with exemptions into major championships and Forrest's win is indicative of the added importance and what makes golf the best — the ability to change your life and career trajectory with one week of excellence.
Land of the rising sun starElsewhere in Japan, a man who was excited to punch his ticket into the Masters via his last victory at the Wyndham Championship won again. That is Michael Brennan, of course. The big-hitting righty continues to impress and continues to make me look smart for wanting him to be on the U.S. Presidents Cup team. Enough about me, though.Brennan picked up his third career victory in his 33rd career PGA Tour start. Brennan is the fourth-fastest player to reach three PGA Tour wins since 1970, behind only Tiger Woods (23 starts), Collin Morikawa (29) and Jerry Pate (32), according to Rick Gehman. He is now the youngest winner of the Baycurrent Classic and the youngest player inside the top 20 of the OWGR at 24 years old.Brennan won thanks to a final-round 68 that was just enough to hold off Keith Mitchell and Jacob Bridgeman by a single stroke. All three of his wins have come via leading at the 54-hole mark, as he is now a perfect 3 of 3 converting leads after three rounds into victories. He did so this time by hitting 55 of 60 fairways, including 15 of 15 in both the second and final rounds.
Europe closes its bordersThe DP World Tour will not grant membership to any player who participates in LIV Golf next year, according to BBC Sport. The immediate impact is apparent, given it is a Ryder Cup year, as those who wish to play for Europe in the biennial event against the Americans must be members of the DP World Tour.And you know what? Good for the DP World Tour.Whatever LIV Golf 2.0 becomes, one thing is for certain: It won't suddenly become meaningful.Those who took the money grab, played exhibition golf for the last few years and ushered in an early retirement should have zero complaints about this move by the DP World Tour, given they have taken from that league over the same timeframe.
It is about time for the DP World Tour to stand up for itself in a real way. The case could be made that the league could strike down in an even more punitive fashion, but this line in the sand will suffice and prompt those contemplating their next career moves to determine whether they want to play real golf or continue down the path of irrelevance.

title: Best of the rest: Pac-12 returns, Mountain West shifts, college hoops Cinderellas to know - CBS Sports
description: Conference realignment has hit the mid-major ranks in a major way this year. The most consequential move of them all is a big-band reviv
body:
Conference realignment has hit the mid-major ranks in a major way this year. The most consequential move of them all is a big-band revival that's got a whole new vibe: The Pac-12 is back and it swiped basically half of the Mountain West on its path to resurrection. The new union out west involves (alphabetically): Boise State, Colorado State, Fresno State, Gonzaga, Oregon State, San Diego State, Texas State, Utah State and Washington State. Yes: nine state schools and Gonzaga.But Gonzaga was absolutely necessary to legitimize the Pac-12 in its morphed, new phase. I'm so very intrigued to see how the Pac-12 fares in its first season under new management. With the NCAA Tournament now (unfortunately) at 76 teams, the conference should have aspirations of getting at least three into the Big Dance on an annual basis. And in 2027, I expect that to be the case. As for the Mountain West, it was able to keep the likes of UNLV, New Mexico and Nevada. It brought Grand Canyon aboard, which feels consequential for that league's hopes of trying to be a two-bid league in the years to come. But with the likes of UC Davis, San Jose State, Hawaii and Air Force still in the ranks, the conference's best days are almost certainly in the past. More moves to know: The WAC is dead and has been rebranded as the United Athletic Conference (umm, OK?) after infusing some former ASUN programs, which has reduced the ASUN to an eight-school outfit. There are some other random one-off jettisons that you can catch all the way up on here. 
Let's take a tour around 27 of the 32 conferences outside the high-major structure and reacquaint you with the players, coaches, programs and trends to know.           Ten players to know           These aren't necessarily the 10 best players outside of the Power Five leagues, but they are certainly 10 guys you should be following over the next five months. Some of them will surely be involved in the NCAA tourney.              1. Braden Huff, GonzagaPretty clearly the best player outside the Power Five. Huff is an efficiency monster who needs to stay healthy the entire season in order to give Gonzaga a shot at a top-three NCAA seed. (Huff played in 18 games last year and was sidelined with a knee injury in January that wound up being more serious than initially disclosed.) The movable 6-10 4-man is surrounded by sturdy reinforcements (returning SF Davis Fogle and center Massamba Diop, by way of Arizona State, could have GU among the best frontcourts in the sport) that could lead to an All-American season in the wake of Graham Ike's departure.
2. Mason Falslev, Utah State  Put him as a top-five player on this list a year ago and he definitely matched the buzz. Falslev was good for 16.0 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 1.9 steals on 51.4% shooting. He's one of the rare talents outside the high-major structure who ranks as a top-50 player in the sport. A terrific guard who opted to stick around in Logan despite losing his coach, Jerrod Calhoun, to Cincinnati. Falslev has teamed up with Ben Jacobsen, who got the job after a long run at Northern Iowa. 3. Lazar Djokovic, VCUThe 6-11 Serbian is slotted to star for the Rams. He no-showed in VCU's blowout loss to Illinois in the second round, but Djokovic put up 13.2 points and 5.2 rebounds in 27.7 minutes per game. His 3-point attempts have gone up each season; will Djokovic be empowered to shoot at least 100 triples in 30-plus games? He's likely to become one of the most productive and valuable mid-major bigs on the scene in '26-27.
                                                                    Keith Gillett/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images
                                                                       4. Trey Green, Saint LouisThough Robbie Avila is trying to sue for one more season with the Billikens, Green is going to ball out regardless of Cream Abdul-Jabbar's 5-for-5 case. SLU has a lot of dudes (Kellen Thames and Amari McCottry could be The Dude on any given night), but Green is prone to pop and up his averages from 10.7 points to closer to 15.0, from 2.9 rebounds to close to five. He also could shoot above 40% from 3-point range again as well for a SLU team eyeing Top 25 status more weeks than not in 2026-27.
           5. Amael L'Etang, DaytonA formidable Frenchie, indeed. Dayton's next big thing is quite literally that: 7-foot-1, 230 pounds and the best center in the Atlantic 10. This is not a ranking of his play from last season, but rather a forecast of what's to come. Because his numbers were fine but nothing spectacular: 11.9 points, 5.9 rebounds, 1.2 blocks per game. They also let the Big Baguette step out and take some triples: L'Etang was 35-of-97 from beyond the arc. Next chapter is going to be a good one.           6. Joshua Dent, Saint Mary'sI've got more on the big changes at SMC below, but at least Dent stuck around to likely thrive in a Gonzaga-less WCC. He stepped up as a sophomore and averaged 13.2 points, 5.6 assists, shot 91.8% from the charity stripe and hit 40% of his 3s. Very good player who will be a top-100 guy if he can handle an even heavier workload with a new head coach running the show.           7. Jake Hall, New MexicoMaybe the best mid-major player that most people don't know about, and that's because he's only one year into what could be an awesome four- or five-year run. Hall was a big find by UNM coach Eric Olen; the forward from Carlsbad, California, averaged better than 16 points and shot 43.8% from deep for a 26-win Lobos team. One of the more crucial retentions at the mid-major level this season. It's because of Hall's loyalty that New Mexico has a shot to make the NCAAs.
    8. J.J. Starling, BuffaloNot nearly enough attention is given to the players who down-transfer and, in the process, can alter their college experience for the better. Starling was at one point considered in the realm of a top-100 talent in this sport. But after three seasons at Syracuse, it never clicked the way so many envisioned. Now he can run the show at Buffalo and might turn the Bulls into the fun dark horse of the MAC.     9. Dylan Darling, Grand CanyonThe hero of St. John's first Sweet 16 trip in 27 years is opting for a massive change of scenery. Going from Queens and Rick Pitino to Phoenix and Bryce Drew is a full-on pendulum swing. Darling was previously at Idaho State, so he figures to find real footing and more consistency with the Mountain West's preseason favorite.
                                                                    Jamie Schwaberow/NCAA Photos via Getty Images
                                                                10. Elijah Price, NevadaThe 6-9 adaptable junior should be the primary piece for the final team coached by Steve Alford. The soon-to-be 62-year-old Alford announced last month that this season would be his last. Look for Price to average somewhere in the neighborhood of 15-and-10 while trying to worm through an easier-to-navigate Mountain West.
           Mid-major coaches on the climb           Every year, I like to spotlight a handful of coaches at mid-majors who are on a path to potentially land a high-major job in the coming year(s). I don't like to repeat coaches on this list within a five-year period, so here's just some who've been highlighted since 2022: Casey Alexander (Belmont), Robert Jones (Norfolk State), Ritchie McKay (Liberty), Bob Richey (Furman), Pat Kelsey (Charleston), Darian DeVries (Drake), Dusty May (FAU), Kenny Blakeney (Howard),  James Jones (Yale), Bucky McMillan (Samford), Josh Schertz (Saint Louis), Takayo Siddle (UNCW) and Tony Skinn (George Mason).  Phil Martelli Jr., VCUHe's just one season in, but what a start in Richmond. The Rams earned their way into the NCAA Tournament, then provided one of the better comebacks against a high-major opponent in the event's history when Martelli's team overcame a 19-point deficit to UNC, the biggest turnaround in the first round by any team — ever. Martelli's got another good group and should see his team dance in 2027.Eric Olen, New MexicoOlen's first three seasons as a head coach were tough — he was 16 games under .500 as of March of 2023 — but he's been one of the more successful mid-major guys the past three years, going 77-28 at UC San Diego and New Mexico. If New Mexico is at least 22 wins-good this season (while playing in a diluted Mountain West, remember) Olen will have a solid shot at the vacant Oregon job — and surely others. He was involved with BC before Luke Murray won out.
Flynn Clayman, High PointIf you're reading this story in October, that means you were definitely watching the NCAA Tournament, which means you don't need to be introduced to Flynn Clayman. Even still, let's enjoy this incredible moment again.
In May, I wrote a story about how Clayman was able to take that moment right there and use it to his advantage for the Panthers' nonconference schedule. High Point claims one of the best treasure chests outside the power-conference structure. We should expect to see them dancing again in 2027. Ryan Miller, Murray StateMurray State has gotten serious about its NIL investments in the past two years, now ranking in the top 15 among all mid-majors. As a result, Miller's going to have the preseason favorites in the Missouri Valley. The Racers went 20-13 last season, Miller's first at the helm after his time as a Creighton assistant. Should Memphis open in 2027, Miller will be on the short list of candidates for that job. 
Speedy Claxton, HofstraThe signature player of Jay Wright's time with the (former) Flying Dutchmen, Claxton has been chipping away and doing a really nice job on Long Island the past five years. He's 105-63 and took his alma mater to last season's NCAA Tournament. The Pride had an elite mid-major duo in the backcourt last season, but alas, Preston Edmead is now at NC State and Cruz Davis got a big check to go play for Texas Tech. Still, Claxton has the goods to eventually bump up.         Sixteen must-know non-Power Five programsHere are a variety of teams to have on your radar before we tip the season on Nov. 1. Expect at least a couple of these squads to be noisemakers in November and December. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. GonzagaNew conference, same story for Gonzaga. The Pac-12's incoming bully will have two high-end returnees (Braden Huff, Davis Fogle) and a slew of transfers. It'd be a shock if Gonzaga wasn't a top-20 program again, though the team is waiting on multiple guys who have not yet been cleared: Xaivian Lee (Florida), Chauncey Wiggins (Florida State), Javon Bennett (Dayton). Arizona State big Massamba Diop might be the portal pickup that proves most crucial to GU's goals of reaching another Sweet 16 (at minimum) and earning a top-four seed. 
The toughness quotient continues with Houston guard Isiah Harwell, plus French point guard Nathan De Sousa, who was borderline necessary after Gonzaga lost Mario Saint-Supery to a mid-July defection back to Spain. Mark Few was inducted into the Naismith Hall of Fame in August. He'll burnish that reputation yet again when Gonzaga makes a 27th consecutive NCAA Tournament. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Saint LouisJosh Schertz was given an eight-figure budget to retain his talent and go out to bring in more to make this one of the best Saint Louis teams ever. The Billikens are waiting on whether Robbie Avila gets cleared, but even if he doesn't, this squad has a chance to be one of the 30 best schools across the next five months. SLU has five of its top seven back, led by Trey Green, Amari McCottry, Kellen Thames and Ishan Sharma. There's so much to be optimistic about here, especially considering the beautiful style of offense Schertz deploys and how well his guys endear themselves to that style. Schertz has 114 wins in his first five seasons at the D-I level. I suspect this is his best one yet.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. VCUIf SLU doesn't win the Atlantic 10, it's probably going to be VCU. The Rams can match the Billikens' returning firepower, led by Lazar Djokovic, Nyk Lewis, Brandon Jennings and Michael Belle. Terrence Hill Jr. is no longer here (he was way too good and Tennessee was going to pay him way too much for him to stay In Richmond), but there's enough talent in the cupboard to expect VCU makes a second straight NCAA tourney under the same coach for the first time since ... Will Wade!
 Last season, Phil Martelli Jr.'s team ranked 51st in offensive and defensive efficiency last season; I'd bank on both of them nudging up. The Rams brought over Blake Harper from Creighton, and I suspect he'll have his best college season yet. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Grand CanyonObligatory opening sentence about the Antelopes having one of the best home-court environments in mid-major — nay, college — basketball. Bryce Drew has built up something sustainable, made all the more viable with GCU's move into the Mountain West. And with a hefty chunk of money to spread around, Grand Canyon brought in transfers from St. John's (Dylan Darling), USC (Amarion Dickerson), Wake Forest (Omaha Biliew) ... and is waiting on two more in five-for-five cases. Last season saw GCU win 20 games in its first year in the Mountain West. Now, with the exodus of SDSU, Boise State, Colorado State and others to the Pac-12, this looks like the best team in the remade MW, even if the big question is how good it can reliably shoot the 3. 
                                                                    Louis Grasse / Getty Images
                                                            
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. San Diego StateAcross the past nine seasons, SDSU's average end-of-year KenPom ranking is a mighty respectable 41st. That's all under Brian Dutcher, who enters his 10th season with a probable top-three team in the Pac-12. With that in mind, Dutcher gets the benefit of the doubt until proven otherwise. The 'Tecs are light on experience but do bring back a pair of starting-level wings in Elzie Harrington and Tae Simmons. Dutcher should mold a tough-as-hell defensive unit again. One player who's going to have the league's attention is Jeremiah Cherry, a center by way of Sacramento State. Biggest question here is if Boston U transfer Chance Gladden can hold up (and lift up) as the point guard for 35 games. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. High PointThe Panthers have some quality players back and a nice influx inbound after winning 31 games and providing one of the few high-major upsets in last season's NCAAs with the vanquishing of 5-seed Wisconsin. Flynn Clayman gets four guys back in the mix in forward Braden Hausen, point guard Conrad Martinez, forward Cam'Ron Fletcher and big man Caden Miller. The two big names to know are lead guard CJ Brown (South Florida) and do-it-all wing Jason Rivera-Torres, who was a stud at Monmouth and could be one of the best mid-major portal adds. The Big South might have the biggest gap between its best team and the rest of the conference; High Point will dance again barring a stunner.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. George MasonThe Patriots haven't yet made an NCAA Tournament under Tony Skinn, but then again it's only been three years. And in that time GMU has established itself as one of the five best teams in the A-10. The Patriots have put up 23.3 wins per year under Skinn. I think the group matches that average this season, even with some new blood and the expected mid-major rebuild amid the portal wars. Look for Brayden O'Connor (who missed last season due to injury) and Mercer transfer Baraka Okojie to be one of the three best backcourts in the league. Experienced, to say the least. James Nnaji's run at Baylor didn't work out, but maybe he'll become a real factor here. GMU also has Lilian Marville coming in to be a spark off the bench, which will be a boost when he likely sinks north of 40% of his 3s after making 52% of them as a flamethrower at UNCG last season.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. New MexicoWhen you're a mid-major these days, I suppose the best you can ask for is to retain two starters who average double-digit scoring. If they're both guards, even better. That's the situation in the ABQ, where the Lobos will bring back all-league talent Jake Hall (16.3 ppg) at the 2 and 5-11 point guard Uriah Tenette (10.7 ppg), who is a terrific two-way player. That pairing alone should give New Mexico optimism for a run in the Mountain West under second-year coach Eric Olen. Former Cal forward Rytis Petraitis projects as one of the better inbound transfers in the conference as well. Some real unknowns with how sturdy the frontcourt can be, and this team's depth, but Olen's been too good to doubt UNM right now as one of the 10 best outside the power-conference structure.
                                                                    Jamie Sabau/NCAA Photos via Getty Images
                                                            
                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. DaytonAnother solid year likely is coming for the Flyers, who have undergone more roster turnover than desired but still should be one of the four best teams in the Atlantic 10. You read above about Ameal L'Etang, who is going to wreck chaos in the conference. He'll have a band of transfers alongside him bolstering Dayton's chances, likely led by former Marquette wing Zaide Lowery. The A-10's best freshman might be Aiden Derkack, a top-75 player in the class who could be a starter midway through the season. One more guy who's got a lot of intrigue here is Jalen Haynes, last seen at George Mason two years ago when he averaged 14 and 7 as a 4-man. If he's back to full strength, this ranking will be too low for UD.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Wichita StateBeen a minute since the Shockers received preseason consideration in a piece like this. Paul Mills just might have Wichita State's first NCAA Tournament team since the 2020-21 COVID year that saw WSU barely squeak in. Mills' team was noticeably better as the season went along in 2025-26, helped by the 7-2 force that is Will Berg. He'll wrap up his college career with a Shockers team that looks to be the best in the American, thanks most of all to Berg. Other important guys who are back include wing TJ Williams and power forward Dillon Battie. If the Shockers are the best rebounding team in the conference (as I suspect will be the case), then they'll have a 1 next to their name with the league tournament tips. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    11. Utah StateReally intrigued to see what Ben Jacobson can do with a change of scenery. He won 397 games at UNI from 2006-26 and patiently waited for a real opportunity. USU has been a revolving door of good coaches for most of the past 15 years. Jacobson looks like the next in line — but I'd bank on him sticking around for close to a decade. He retains Mason Falslev, giving him the rare kind of talent a coach can inherit at the mid-major level. The other returnee is forward Karson Templin, who should boost up to being a 12-and-6 guy this season. Center Will Hornseth followed along from UNI, while the player who's waiting for five-for-five eligibility clearance (who could knock the Aggies into the top 50) is Dallin Hall. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    12. Saint Mary'sAfter 25 years, Randy Bennett is no longer running the show in Moraga. (He took the Arizona State job, as you likely knew.) It's going to be strange to see SMC without Bennett on the sidelines, and also SMC in a WCC that doesn't include Gonzaga. Former Gaels guard Mickey McConnell is now the coach. Can he get Saint Mary's a regular-season title in Year 1? Santa Clara seems to be the biggest competition, but McConnell is blessed with the league's best point guard: Joshua Dent. A minutes monster who you can read more about above, Dent will have full reign over the offense on a team with a lot of parts to figure out. This is a forecast based on Saint Mary's culture. McConnell will have his work cut out for him right away.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    13. NevadaElijah Price, Vaughn Weems and Peyton White are the three rotation players who will run it back in Steve Alford's final season. They combined to average 28 points last season on a team that won 24 games but lacked the week-over-week consistency in league play to vault them to the NCAA Tournament. Price is so talented, he'll help overcome some of Nevada's weaknesses. I'm not seeing a team that's going to be dangerous as a shooting group, but I do think Alford's last hurrah and the positionless attack will make Nevada good enough to be fighting for an at-large bid entering the Mountain West bracket.
                                                                    Greg Ashman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images

Konkol worked the portal to bring in guys via Seton Hall, Creighton, Missouri State, UTSA and beyond. Last season's team made it all the way to the NIT title game. I don't think this year's group is quite as strong offensively, but a top-three finish in the American should be the expectation.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    15. George WashingtonYeah, the A-10 is going to be a three-bid league this season. With 76 slots available and this much talent influx into the league and the spending that was committed, it's hard to see how the conference fails to get at least two of the 44 best at-large candidates. GW should be in that mix after bringing board wing Omari Weatherspoon from Pitt, wing Terrence Arceneaux from NC State (is this when he FINALLY breaks out?), big man Dylan James from Georgia and backup big Andrija Vukovic from Oklahoma State. The majority of the rotation will be juniors, seniors and grad transfers. Coach Chris Caputo has his most rugged defensive roster yet, which should equate to his best team in the District.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    16. MemphisPenny Hardaway hasn't had a season without serious turbulence since ... ? Brace for more in 2026-27, as the Tigers don't rate anywhere near top-50 status, yet scheduled like they're a Sweet 16 squad. Iowa State, VCU, Vanderbilt, Louisville, Dayton, Baylor, Grand Canyon and Texas are all on Memphis' docket in the first seven weeks of the season. Hardaway clearly did this with the hopes that his team can scrounge up enough good non-con wins to overcome what's likely to be a one-bid American. He also did this after winning only 13 games last season. The player with the highest expectations is Northwestern transfer Jayden Reid, a 5-10 point guard who will team up in the backcourt with Pitt transfer Brandin Cummings. title: Penny Hardaway contributed $2.6 million of his own money to Memphis' $9 million revenue sharing - CBS Sports
description: Hardaway is entering his ninth season as Memphis' head coach. He is the latest college basketball coach to donate
body:
Hardaway is entering his ninth season as Memphis' head coach. He is the latest college basketball coach to donate back to his team's revenue sharing.

                    at
    2:03 pm ET

        At American Conference Media Day on Monday in Tampa, Memphis coach Penny Hardaway said that he contributed $2.6 million of his own money toward his team's revenue sharing for the 2026-27 season. Hardaway told the Commercial Appeal that Memphis' total revenue-sharing amount this season is $9 million."They didn't ask me to do it, they were saying if you want more money, you have to put your money in. So I did," Hardaway told Jason Munz of the Commercial Appeal. "I didn't want to fail two years in a row, because I already know what that means for me. Because it's already like the death sentence for me from so many different people, which is hilarious."The Tigers finished 13-19 (8-10 in the American) and missed the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 2024, which turned the temperature up on his seat. Before that, Hardaway had guided Memphis to three appearances in the big dance in four years before finishing with the least amount of wins in a single season since the 1999-00 campaign.Memphis had a busy offseason retooling its roster and landed nine transfers, including Pitt guard Brandin Cummings and Washington State forward Rihard Vavers. The Tigers also landed four-star guard Fred Smith Jr., who was the No. 97-ranked player in the 2026 recruiting cycle by 247Sports.
Hardaway admitting he contributed his own money to his team's basketball roster is a sign of the times, but he isn't the only coach to redirect his personal funds toward revenue sharing. DePaul coach Chris Holtmann told CBS Sports' Matt Norlander at Big East Media Day that he took a lower salary in his contract extension in order to redirect funds toward revenue sharing.
"Let's change the last couple of years, really for Years 5, 6 and 7, let's change the structure of the contract where I'm making less money," Holtmann said. "I think for me the most important thing is being competitive and in order to be competitive, we need to raise NIL. ... It was pretty significant that I did that. I told my agent I did it and the AD had agreed to it, and he goes, 'What are you doing?'"
Last season, Utah State coach Jerrod Calhoun donated $150,000 to his school's NIL fund. Utah State reached the NCAA Tournament back-to-back seasons under Calhoun's watch before he departed this offseason to become the coach at Cincinnati.

These are determined during qualifying racing, which typically takes place the day before the race. You can also bet on markets offering odds for who will finish in the top 5 or top 10 in qualifying, though these aren't necessarily  available for every race. The results of qualifying will often shift the race odds.Motor sports futures bettingFormula 1 bettingIn most cases, F1 futures usually apply to the next race. However, you can bet on season-long futures for F1 championship betting. The Drivers Championship is straightforward as it will be given to the driver who accumulates the most points over the season. The Constructors Championship takes into account the points for both team drivers. Only the top 10 finishers in each race score points, and those points are tallied over the season. The winning driver can be part of a constructors championship, but that's not always the case.NASCAR BettingNASCAR has different portions of the season. While you can't pick multiple drivers to win an event in a parlay, you can pick multiple drivers to finish in the top 5 or top 10. You can also pick teams to finish in the top 5 or top 10.How to bet on motor sports live during a raceSportsbooks do offer live odds for motor sports, though this is likely a more prominent feature for NASCAR and IndyCar as opposed to F1. Driver and team odds will shift based on where they are in the grand scheme of the race. NASCAR and IndyCar allow for more leeway since there are more laps, while F1 can sometimes shift quickly towards one driver or team.Tips and strategies for how to bet on motor sportsDriver form does matter when it comes to racing, but the biggest predictor of success is usually how each team can adjust to conditions. Races can take place in all kinds of weather and team strategy can make or break the day. There are some teams that struggle to adjust, and bettors should know which teams those are before placing wagers. Historical track success often takes a back seat to current form. If the wreck is too big to clear in a reasonable amount of time, the race will end despite the caution flag being signaled. Overtime doesn't really exist, but usually there will be at least one additional lap of racing should the fallout of the crash get removed in a timely manner and the safety car gets taken off the track.FAQCan you bet on motor sports?As long as you are of legal age in a state where sports betting is legitimate, you should be able to find a sportsbook which provides racing and motor sports odds.Who to bet on for the Indy 500?Because the Indy 500 typically takes place over Memorial Day weekend, you'll have to wait for a bit before placing wagers on who will win the signature event.         The latest injury in Michael Penix Jr.'s snakebitten career was particularly cruel not only for him but for his team, too. Penix took a hard hit to his ribs late in regulation, knocking him out for overtime of the Falcons' eventual 30-23 loss to the Ravens on "Sunday Night Football."Penix's injury is not considered serious, according to ESPN, who added that he could potentially play in Sunday's game against the Bears. Atlanta plans to exercise caution, however, and will monitor his practice this week before making a decision on his status for Week 6. Here's the hit from Tavius Robinson that caused Penix's injury:
Initially, Penix missed just one play — the one immediately following the hit — when Tua Tagovailoa entered the game and found Bijan Robinson for a 14-yard gain on second-and-20. Penix returned and threw a ball away under pressure, and the Falcons punted to end regulation.The Ravens took the ball to start overtime and produced a touchdown drive that lasted over seven minutes. Cameras panned multiple times to the sideline, where Atlanta's medical staff was working on/examining Penix's right ribs. When Atlanta came out on offense, Tagovailoa entered while Penix had a towel over his head, distraught as he could only watch from the sideline. After the game, Penix said he was emotional because he wants to finish games and is frustrated by how many times he hasn't been able to do so.
"I did take some throws on the sideline just to see how I felt, and I did not feel like I was gonna be able to give our team what we needed to help us win that football game because of the pain that I was feeling, so that's all that happened," Penix said. "I was trying to get out there. [I] feel like if we had the ball first in overtime, I probably would have been out there, but as we were sitting, what I was going through, it just started getting worse and worse as we were just sitting there. I was getting cold."Tagovailoa found Drake London for 20 yards on Atlanta's first offensive play of overtime, but got picked off by Kyle Hamilton on the next snap.
Though Kevin Stefanski said the team will need to conduct more imaging and testing before establishing a timeline for Penix's return, Penix speaking to the media is a good sign.
"Knowing me, I'mma be ready to go next week because I've sat out enough my career," Penix said. "... I will work my tail off to make sure I'm back out there on that field."Michael Penix Jr. injury historySeason/TeamInjury2018/Indiana   HoosiersRight   torn ACL2019/Indiana   HoosiersFractured   collarbone2020/Indiana   HoosiersRight   torn ACL2021/Washington   HuskiesLeft   A/C joint separation2025/Atlanta   FalconsLeft   knee bone bruise, partially torn ACL      Penix, who missed the first two games of the season, had been a huge reason Atlanta turned its season around from 0-2 to 2-2 and is still afloat now at 2-3. The Falcons have now had four different quarterbacks play this season already: Penix, Tagovailoa, Cooper Rush (who started the first two games) and Jack Strand (who relieved a struggling Rush in a 34-3 loss in Week 2).Penix's ability to push the ball downfield helped free up the running game and make the passing game, mainly through London, come to life. The Falcons would very much like Penix's self-diagnosed availability for Week 6 to be accurate, given how much the team has struggled without him.

        Alabama wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams is unlikely to play against No. 14 Tennessee as he deals with multiple injuries, coach Kalen DeBoer announced on Monday. Coleman-Williams is reportedly dealing with both leg and head injuries after the No. 6 Crimson Tide's loss to Georgia. "[Coleman-Williams] has got a couple things going on," DeBoer said. "Got to work through an injury with the knee that's been kind of going on. We'll deal with that. Got the head issue as well. Gonna address that, even the lower extremity there, this week. Pretty good chance we wouldn't have him this weekend. Probably be week-to-week after that." Coleman-Williams was hit in the head and had to be helped off the field multiple times during the 20-17 loss to the Bulldogs on Saturday. The final hit was from Georgia safety KJ Bolden in the fourth quarter, from which he did not return. Coleman-Williams also wore a brace over his right knee during the past two games. The junior has put together a resurgent season at Alabama, catching 23 passes for 415 yards and four touchdowns. He had three catches for 39 yards before going out against the Bulldogs. Last season, Coleman-Williams posted five catches for 87 yards in a 37-20 win over Tennessee. 
With Coleman-Williams sidelined, Alabama could employ more of a committee approach to wide receiver.
